input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)
input.rationale: Section 6.1 binds the Company (our client) with a field-of-use non-compete. It is term-only with no post-term tail (so not walk-away territory, unlike the reciprocal two-year restriction on HDI in Section 6.3), but it fails the fallback on two material terms: the scope is not limited to a named competing product — it reaches "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled", an elastic standard covering our core leather apparel line; and there is no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (Section 6.2 carves out only a closeout-merchandise site, and the Deerskin Products definition excludes the Joan Cook Catalog). Because HDI's exclusive hosting bargain plausibly needs some protection, we propose the fallback narrowing rather than outright deletion: limit the restriction to Deerskin Products and add carve-outs for other products, internal development and acquired businesses. We note the one-year term auto-renews annually, so the restriction can run past 12 months; we have left that alone as it is coextensive with the deal and terminable on 90 days' notice.

proposal.summary: Narrow Section 6.1 non-compete on the Company to Deerskin Products only and add carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we sell, so we have narrowed Section 6.1 to the named Deerskin Products that are the subject of the Site and removed the open-ended "substantially similar products/companies" language. We have also added carve-outs for our own internal development and for acquired businesses; the restriction remains in force for the term, which preserves HDI's exclusivity bargain.

ops.newText: for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet. Nothing in this Section 6.1 shall restrict the Company from (i) offering or selling any products other than Deerskin Products through any channel, (ii) internally developing web sites or e-commerce capabilities, or (iii) continuing to operate any business or web site acquired by, or merged with, the Company or any of its affiliates.
